records.text: The supplied report excerpt said a SAR entry dated around 2020-05-15 recorded Conservative MP David Davis’s pandemic-modelling criticism as “critical of the government.” The excerpt connected this to Davis’s tweets and a Daily Telegraph article co-written with Lord Ridley questioning the Imperial College model’s code and mathematical assumptions, while arguing that they called for transparency and scrutiny rather than asserting the model was necessarily wrong. The report criticized monitoring Davis for parliamentary scrutiny as unjustifiable and a threat to free speech and accountability.

The excerpt said the CDU monitored the creation of Parler accounts by three unnamed Conservative MPs in summer 2020, despite no indication that their accounts posted material of significant government interest. It also said some current and former ministers were affected by CDU activities relating to pandemic-policy criticism but were not named in the report.

The excerpt said Logically repeatedly included journalist Julia Hartley-Brewer’s tweets in its COVID-19 Mis/Disinformation Platform Terms of Service Report commissioned by DCMS. Examples included sharing an interview with a listener harmed by lockdown and discussing cancer deaths and reduced cancer referrals during the NHS’s COVID-19 focus. The report argued that these were policy criticism and discussion of documented lockdown harms, not disinformation, and that Logically had stretched the meaning of disinformation.
entities: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport

records.text: The excerpt said Logically included Big Brother Watch Advocacy Manager Mark Johnson’s tweet urging people to sign an official parliamentary petition against COVID-19 vaccine passports, and a talkRADIO interview clip featuring Big Brother Watch director Silkie Carlo opposing COVID passes, in disinformation-related reports shared with DCMS. At the time, the petition had over 275,000 signatures, the government was consulting on the policy, and opposition was shared by many MPs. The excerpt said the criticism concerned human rights and equality, not vaccine claims, and questioned why dissent on a live policy debate was being monitored.
entities: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport

records.text: The excerpt said Logically characterized Silkie Carlo’s comparison of vaccine-passport enforcement and impact with mandatory vaccination as a potential breach of Twitter’s terms of service, alleging that it distorted facts and supported a narrative that passports were mandatory vaccination. The report argued that Carlo’s comparison was factually accurate, did not claim passports would inevitably lead to mandatory vaccines, and was protected commentary under Twitter’s then-current medical misinformation policy. The excerpt characterized this as misrepresentation and potential flagging of protected speech for censorship.
records.topic: Silkie Carlo tweet and Twitter terms of service

records.text: The excerpt said an August 2021 CDU report titled “Vaccine Mis/Disinformation: Narratives and Engagement” named pub landlord and political commentator Adam Brooks for opposing vaccine passports and compulsory vaccination, while not opposing vaccination itself. The report described him as a vaccine and lockdown sceptic. The excerpt criticized this as an overly broad treatment of policy dissent as disinformation and argued that such labeling could delegitimize criticism.

On 2023-01-15, the assistant summarized the excerpt’s claims that Logically monitored David Davis’s modelling criticism, monitored three unnamed Conservative MPs’ Parler activity, and reported Julia Hartley-Brewer’s government-critical tweets; it said the excerpt viewed this monitoring as unjustifiable remit expansion threatening free speech and parliamentary scrutiny.
